PARTICIPATION AT CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY/ORANGE COUNTY GREAT PARK BOARD MEETINGS
MEETINGS ARE BROADCAST LIVE ON ICTV, COX COMMUNICATIONS LOCAL ACCESS CHANNEL 30, AND AT&T U-VERSE CHANNEL 99, AND LIVESTREAMED ONLINE AT CITYOFIRVINE.ORG/ICTV. YOU MAY SUBMIT COMMENTS ON ANY AGENDA ITEM OR ON ANY ITEM NOT ON THE AGENDA, IN WRITING VIA MAIL TO “ATTN: CITY COUNCIL,” ONE CIVIC CENTER PLAZA, IRVINE, CA 92606; BY EMAIL TO CLERK@CITYOFIRVINE.ORG; OR THROUGH E-COMMENT AT CITYOFIRVINE.ORG/ICTV. YOU MAY ALSO PROVIDE LIVE COMMENTS VIA “ZOOM.” FOR MORE INFORMATION, VISIT CITYOFIRVINE.ORG/ICTV AND SELECT “CITY COUNCIL MEETINGS.”
REQUEST TO SPEAK IN PERSON: IF YOU WOULD LIKE TO ADDRESS THE CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY/ORANGE COUNTY GREAT PARK BOARD ON A SCHEDULED AGENDA ITEM – INCLUDING A CONSENT CALENDAR ITEM, A REGULAR COUNCIL/BOARD BUSINESS ITEM, A PUBLIC HEARING ITEM, OR PUBLIC COMMENTS – PLEASE REGISTER BY COMPLETING THE ELECTRONIC FORM AVAILABLE ON THE KIOSK AT THE ENTRANCE TO THE CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER. PLEASE IDENTIFY ON THE FORM YOUR NAME AND THE ITEM ON WHICH YOU WOULD LIKE TO SPEAK. THE REQUEST TO SPEAK FORM ON THE KIOSK ASSISTS THE MAYOR/CHAIR IN ENSURING THAT ALL PERSONS WISHING TO ADDRESS THE CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY/ORANGE COUNTY GREAT PARK BOARD ARE RECOGNIZED. IT ALSO ENSURES THE ACCURATE IDENTIFICATION OF MEETING PARTICIPANTS IN THE CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY/ORANGE COUNTY GREAT PARK BOARD MINUTES. YOUR NAME WILL BE CALLED AT THE TIME THE MATTER IS HEARD BY THE CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY/ORANGE COUNTY GREAT PARK BOARD. CITY POLICY IS TO LIMIT PUBLIC TESTIMONY TO UP TO THREE MINUTES PER SPEAKER DEPENDING ON RELEVANT CIRCUMSTANCES (UNLESS THE TIME LIMIT IS EXTENDED BY THE MAYOR/CHAIR), WHICH INCLUDES THE PRESENTATION OF ELECTRONIC OR AUDIO VISUAL INFORMATION. SPEAKERS MAY NOT YIELD THEIR TIME TO OTHER PERSONS.
PLEASE TAKE NOTICE THAT THE ORDER OF SCHEDULED AGENDA ITEMS BELOW AND/OR THE TIME THEY ARE ACTUALLY HEARD, CONSIDERED AND DECIDED MAY BE MODIFIED BY THE MAYOR/CHAIR OR THE CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY/ORANGE COUNTY GREAT PARK BOARD DURING THE COURSE OF THE MEETING, SO PLEASE STAY ALERT.
PLEASE NOTE: THE CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY/ORANGE COUNTY GREAT PARK BOARD IS MAKING EVERY EFFORT TO FOLLOW THE SPIRIT AND INTENT OF THE BROWN ACT AND OTHER APPLICABLE LAWS REGULATING THE CONDUCT OF PUBLIC MEETINGS, IN ORDER TO MAXIMIZE TRANSPARENCY AND PUBLIC ACCESS. FOR QUESTIONS OR ASSISTANCE, PLEASE CONTACT THE CITY CLERK’S OFFICE AT 949-724-6205, OR VIA EMAIL AT CLERK@CITYOFIRVINE.ORG. IT WOULD BE APPRECIATED IF WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS OF PUBLIC COMMENTS RELATED TO ITEMS ON THE AGENDA, OR ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA, ARE PROVIDED PRIOR TO THE COMMENCEMENT OF THE MEETING.

NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC
LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council/Successor Agency meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council/Successor Agency meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 7 p.m. until the next City Council meeting. Regular Orange County Great Park Board meetings are broadcast live every 4th Tuesday of the month at 2 p.m. and are replayed on Wednesdays at 8 p.m., Thursdays at 10 a.m., and Saturdays at 7 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live Orange County Great Park meeting) until the next Orange County Great Park Board meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council/Successor Agency meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv. For more information, please contact the Clerk of the Board/City Clerk's office at (949) 724-6205.
ADJOURNMENT
At 11:00 p.m., the City Council will determine which of the remaining agenda items can be considered and acted upon prior to 12:00 midnight and will continue all other items on which additional time is required until a future City Council meeting. All meetings are scheduled to terminate at 12:00 midnight.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are on file with the City Clerk/Clerk of the Board and are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 12 hours prior to a regular City Council/Successor Agency/Great Park Board meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org and the Orange County Great Park website at ocgp.org at least 12 days prior to the scheduled City Council/Successor Agency/Orange County Great Park Board meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk/Clerk of the Board staff at (949)724-6205.
SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL RECEIVED AFTER THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA
Any supplemental writings or documents distributed to a majority of the City Council/Successor Agency/Orange County Great Park Board regarding any item on this agenda after the posting of the agenda will be available for public review in the City Clerk/Clerk of the Board's Office, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California, during normal business hours. In addition, such writings or documents will be made available for public review at the respective public meeting.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk/Clerk of the Board staff at (949)724-6205.
SUBMITTAL OF INFORMATION BY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC FOR DISSEMINATION OR PRESENTATION AT PUBLIC MEETINGS
Media Types and Guidelines
1. Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting or at the time he/she addresses the City Council/Orange County Great Park Board/Successor Agency. Please provide 15 copies of the information to be submitted and file with the City Clerk at the time of arrival to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council/Orange County Great Park Board/Successor Agency at the time testimony is given.
2. Large Displays/Maps/Renderings:
Any member of the public who desires to display freestanding large displays or renderings in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to notify the City Clerk’s Office at (949)724-6205 no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting so that an easel can be made available, if necessary.
3. Electronic Documents/Audio-Visuals:
Any member of the public who desires to display information electronically in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to submit the information to the Public Information Office (PIO) no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting. To facilitate your request contact the PIO Office at (949)724-6253 or the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Information must be provided on CD, DVD, or VHS; or, emailed by 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting to pio@cityofirvine.org. Members of the public will be asked to provide their name, identify the meeting and the agenda item to be addressed, and a day time phone number.
The PIO office will notify the person submitting the information as soon as possible prior to the meeting if the information cannot be accessed or if the version provided is incompatible with the City's system. Every effort will be made by City staff to facilitate the presentation.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk/Clerk of the Board's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.

  Irvine, CA 92606
CALL TO ORDER
The regular meeting of the Irvine City Council and regular joint meeting with the City of
Irvine as Successor Agency to the dissolved Irvine Redevelopment Agency was called to
order at 4:45 p.m. on August 10, 2021, in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center,
One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California; Mayor/Chairwoman Khan presiding.
ROLL CALL
  Present: 5 Councilmember/Boardmember  Larry Agran
  Councilmember/Boardmember  Mike Carroll
  Councilmember/Boardmember  Anthony Kuo
  Vice Mayor/Vice Chairwoman  Tammy Kim
  Mayor/Chairwoman  Farrah N. Khan

Mayor/Chairwoman Khan announced that City Hall was now open to the public, allowing
members of the public to physically attend and participate in City Council meetings, and
noted the current guidelines for face coverings. She also noted that 1) the meeting was
broadcast live on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and AT&T U-Verse
Channel 99, and livestreamed online at cityofirvine.org; 2) members of the public would
continue to have the ability to provide live comments on agenda items via Zoom; and 3)
the City of Irvine continued to sanitize surfaces and equipment in the Council Chamber
and throughout City Hall.
 City Council Minutes  August 10, 2021

  In addition, Carl Petersen, City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary, provided instructions
  on how to participate in the meeting; and noted that the e-comment feature had been
  extended, which allowed members of the public the ability to submit e-comments on all
  agenda items, which would be included as part of the official record and uploaded to the
  City’s website.

  Mayor/Chairwoman Khan also announced that general public comments for the City
  Council on items not on the agenda would be considered at approximately 6:30 p.m.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Councilmember Kuo led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  INVOCATION

  Pastor Frank Winans from Woodbridge Community Church provided the invocation.

  1.  PRESENTATIONS

  1.1  Irvine Community Land Trust

  Mayor Khan introduced Mark Asturias, Executive Director, Irvine
  Community Land Trust (Land Trust), who provided a brief overview of the
  organization, its accomplishments to date, and future affordable housing
  projects.

  City Council discussion included: noting opportunities provided by the
  Land Trust all levels of income; and expressed appreciation to the Board
  and Executive Director Asturias for leading the Mandel and Horwitz
  homes project for residents with intellectual disabilities.

  Joyce Jin, Irvine resident, spoke in support of affordable housing; and
  questioned whether the City had a plan for traffic improvements if
  additional units continue to be built.

  1.2  State Legislative Advocate Quarterly Update

  Mayor Khan introduced Cori Takkinen, Vice President, Townsend Public
  Affairs, who provided a brief legislative update.

  City Council discussion included: expressing concern about the Regional
  Housing Needs Assessment (RHNA) numbers; inquired about whether
  funding would be available to support cities required to comply with
  Assembly Bill 339; questioned whether the City would be able to seek
  direct funding for the Homeless Housing Assistance and Prevention
  Program (HHAP); and inquired about whether direct access for funding
  would be available for broadband initiatives.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  2
 City Council Minutes  August 10, 2021

  Kevin Corrigan, Irvine resident, spoke in support of continuing the use of
  Zoom and closed captioning for participation in meetings; spoke in
  opposition to the RHNA numbers allocated to the City; and spoke in
  support of the Municipal Broadband Study.

  1.3  Crime Status Update and Opportunities for Community Engagement
  in Crime Prevention

  This item was agendized at the request of Mayor Khan and
  Councilmember Kuo, who noted concerns raised by community
  members about a recent rise in crime.

  Mike Hamel, Director of Public Safety/Chief of Police, and Darcy Jones,
  Business Services Administrator, provided a brief presentation and
  responded to questions.

  City Council discussion included: questioning why repeat offenders are
  released back into the community; inquired about how a community could
  request private security from their homeowners association (HOA);
  questioned different programs available to prevent theft of catalytic
  converters; and inquired about whether automatic license plate readers
  had been utilized to help identify crimes.

  INTERIM CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  There was no report.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  Councilmember Agran provided participated in a community meeting on July 28
  regarding the operations of the All American Asphalt plant, and expressed appreciation
  to community members Kim Conte, Lesley Tan, Tom Hazard, and UCI Professor
  Emeritus Dean Baker for their efforts in organizing the meeting.

  Councilmember Kuo expressed his appreciation to Eagle Scout Parin Ladva, who along
  with friends and supporters, built a courtyard within the Food and Farm Lab at the Great
  Park to highlight a 9/11 survivor tree; and congratulated Daniel Shemtob, University High
  School graduate and Owner/Chef of the Lime Truck, who recently won the Great Food
  Truck Race on the Food Network. He also provided an update on the City of Irvine/Irvine
  Unified School District (IUSD) Liaison Committee meeting, where the Committee was

  o  Cultural and Community

  The winners in each category will be revealed in the winter issue of Inside Irvine,
  and will be featured in an exhibition at the Irvine Civic Center. A grand prize winner
  will receive a $250 gift card to the Irvine Spectrum Center. Submissions will be

  •  The City is pleased to be joining Senator Dave Min at the Cypress Community
  Center where he will be presenting the City with a $14.5 million check for the
  completion of the Jeffrey Open Space Trail (JOST). The JOST currently stretches
  3.5 miles through the heart of the City. The gap closure is a critical element of the
  regions open space plan, and will link existing bike and pedestrian trails,
  connecting the coastline to the Santa Ana Mountains and Cleveland National
  Forest. The 1.3 mile section will run from Barranca to Walnut and will include a 15-
  foot wide bridge stretching almost 2,000 feet from beginning to end. Construction
  is expected to begin next summer and is anticipated to take approximately 18
  months.

  •  In honor of the City’s 50th anniversary and as part of the Diversity, Equity, and
  Inclusion initiative, the City is collaborating with the South Coast Chinese Cultural
  Center to offer a new lecture series for Chinese-Irvine newcomers. The “We Are
  Irvine: Living Resource Guide Series” will highlight lessons learned from Chinese
  American immigrants and Irvine residents. It will support new residents by
  minimizing anxieties due to language barriers, misunderstandings, or other
  unknowns. The lectures will also assist the Chinese-Irvine newcomers with
  efficiently navigating and connecting to resources within the City. The first lecture
  will be August 26. The nine-lecture series will be held bimonthly and will be
  presented in Mandarin. The City is grateful to Principal Yulan Chung for her vision
  and partnership in helping to create the series and it is the City’s hope that through
  its efforts, all residents will feel they are an integral part of the Irvine community.
  For more information about the series and the Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion
  initiative, visit weareirvine.org.

  •  Following the Silverado Fire and the evacuation of nearly 90,000 Irvine residents
  last October, the Irvine Police Department determined the need to expand the use
  of evacuation zones beyond just those communities threatened by wildland fires.
  The City has developed a new map that now includes all-hazard evacuation zones
  for the entire City. Irvine residents are encouraged to become familiar with their
  evacuation zone prior to an emergency. In addition, the City will use this map in
  real-time during emergencies to communicate zones under evacuation or shelter-
  in-place orders. Residents can review the Evacuation Zone Map at
  cityofirvine.org/prepare.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  4

  •  The City of Irvine’s strategic priorities continue to focus on five areas of importance

  o  Quality of Life

  In alignment with the City’s strategic priorities, the City will soon be launching a
